text: A psalm of Asaph. God takes his stand in the assembly of God; in the midst of the gods he renders judgment:

versions.text: A psalm of Asaph. God takes his stand in the divine assembly; among the gods he renders judgment:
versions.explanation: The Hebrew is literally 'in the assembly of El (God)'; 'divine assembly' is a reasonable rendering but obscures the divine name. A footnote could also note that 'gods' (elohim) may refer to rulers or judges, which would help the reader given verses 6-7.

text: "How long will you judge unjustly and lift up the face of the wicked? Selah

versions.text: "How long will you judge unjustly and show favor to the wicked? Selah
versions.explanation: Optional: the idiom 'lift up the face' is the Hebrew image for partiality; 'show favor' is acceptable and clearer for oral reading, so this is only a stylistic note. If retained, consider a footnote explaining 'Selah' as a musical or liturgical pause, since it interrupts the flow when read aloud.

text: Give justice to the weak and the fatherless; uphold the cause of the afflicted and the destitute.
Rescue the poor and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked."

versions.text: Rescue the weak and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked."
versions.explanation: 'dal' is rendered 'weak' in both verse 3 and verse 4, but here the pairing with 'ebyon' (needy) suggests 'poor'; varying the wording also avoids monotony in oral reading. Note the closing quotation mark placement is fine, since God's speech ends here.

text: They neither know nor understand; they walk about in darkness; all the foundations of the earth are shaken.

versions.text: They neither know nor understand; they walk about in darkness, while all the foundations of the earth are shaken.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has three parallel clauses with no conjunction; 'while' adds an interpretive link not in the text. Removing it preserves the abrupt parallelism and reads with better rhythm.

text: I said, "You are gods, sons of the Most High, all of you.
Yet you will die like mere men; you will fall like any prince."
Rise up, O God, and judge the earth, for you shall inherit all the nations.

versions.text: Rise up, O God, and judge the earth, for all the nations belong to you.
versions.explanation: The verb 'tinḥal' means 'you will inherit / take possession as your heritage'; the current rendering flattens the verb into a statement of ownership and loses the future/eschatological force of God's claim upon the nations.
